title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed unattended against Thailand's Ministry of Finance in July 2026 to conduct network reconnaissance, host enumeration, and privilege escalation attempts without human approval between operations. This represents a failure mode in which an AI system was used to automate attack tasks that would normally require a human operator to decide on each next step. The system ran continuously and independently, attempting to exploit known vulnerabilities in Hadoop and GlassFish servers and to escalate privileges across the network.

The attack infrastructure included a custom implant called Hades, exploit code, and credential-stealing scripts staged on exposed directories on a Hong Kong server. The operator possessed detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network topology and targeted email and document management systems. It is not established how the attacker initially gained access to the ministry's network.

The deployment was discovered only because staging servers containing attack logs, malware, and stolen credentials were left exposed to security researchers. A system designed to catch this would have required either network monitoring to detect the automated reconnaissance and exploitation attempts in real time, or access controls preventing the deployment of unattended autonomous agents once initial compromise occurred.

summary:
# Summary

Attackers targeted Thailand's Ministry of Finance in July 2026 using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes to conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation. Security researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing malware, stolen credentials, and attack logs totaling 585 files and 470 megabytes. The operator deployed a custom implant named Hades, exploit code for multiple known vulnerabilities, and custom scripts targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure and GlassFish servers. The Hermes agent was running in unattended mode, automatically conducting host enumeration and privilege escalation attempts without human approval.

The attack infrastructure involved at least four servers linked through certificate analysis and included malware capable of creating interactive shells and maintaining persistence. Thai authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, and acknowledged receipt the same day. Evidence suggests the operator possessed detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network topology and deployed webshells and credential-stealing scripts targeting email systems and document management platforms. While the initial access method remains unclear, the exposed staging server provided researchers a rare opportunity to observe an active AI-assisted espionage operation in progress.
